title: Shared bounded path trie for workspace file events: implementation, tests and landing
outcome: Deliver the shared bounded workspace notification implementation with complete consumer handling, validation and landing evidence, while the parent retains the post-restart baseline and live-host investigation.
acceptance: The measured inefficiencies (unbounded pre-filter channel, per-scope fan-out of each path, pending map that flushes only after 250 ms of quiet) are fixed, and the fix's effect is measured with the same synthetic workload before and after; reports keep established facts separate from the remaining hypothesis about the incident's full 26 GB growth.

Pending workspace file events are held in one bounded structure shared across sessions and scopes, a trie keyed by path components: repeated changes to one path merge, and a subtree whose pending entries exceed a fixed bound collapses to a single directory-level marker. No change notification is lost: every consumer, at least the UI panels (diff, source, git, file tree) and the Engram check-credit fences (watcher order, change-after-launch), still receives the exact path or a covering directory marker, with the fences' ordering guarantees preserved. A written inventory names each consumer with its code location and how it handles a directory marker.
Host memory stays bounded when a project tree receives a burst of file activity, for example tens of thousands of files created or deleted under .tmp. An automated test asserts it.
